title: Empowering Advisors with Tools for the Future of Financial Planning
summary: We were brought in to conduct a deep-dive investigation into the risk insurance journey for a major client. The process was complex, involving multiple touchpoints and stakeholders, and the organization needed clarity on where the experience was breaking down and how to fix it.
imageAlt: Illustrative perspective lattice with connected nodes
context: A deep-dive investigation into the risk insurance journey — complex, with multiple touchpoints and stakeholders.

challenge.lead: Where is the experience breaking down — and how do we fix it?
challenge.body: The organisation needed clarity across a journey involving multiple touchpoints and stakeholders.

approach.title: Visualise the experience
approach.text: A detailed Customer Journey Map documenting interactions across onboarding, identifying pain points and opportunities to simplify, support, and personalise the journey for greater impact.

roadmap.title: Hyper-personalised onboarding flows
roadmap.text: Onboarding that responds to the person, not the process.

roadmap.title: Unified digital adviser handover tools
roadmap.text: One connected handover between the people involved.

roadmap.title: Application progress tracking
roadmap.text: Customers able to see where their application stands.

roadmap.title: Mobile-friendly experiences
roadmap.text: Journeys that work where customers actually are.

built: A proposed roadmap addressing hyper-personalised onboarding flows, unified digital adviser handover tools, customer access to application progress tracking, and mobile-friendly experiences.
reflection: Customers no longer compare your service solely to direct competitors — they measure it against the seamless experiences offered by companies like Amazon, Netflix, and Uber.

result.headline: A clear roadmap for where the journey breaks — and how to fix it.
result.note: This engagement delivered research and a proposed roadmap; no quantified outcomes have been published.

takeaways: Journey maps make the invisible breaking points visible.
Customers benchmark against the best experiences they have, not just your sector.
Adviser tools and customer tools should be designed as one system.
